description: The Pan Niger Delta Forum on Tuesday declared that it has not declared support for any presidential candidate for the 2027 general election, urging voters in the South-South to ...
content:
The Pan Niger Delta Forum on Tuesday declared that it has not declared support for any presidential candidate for the 2027 general election, urging voters in the South-South to choose leaders based on their capacity to advance the interests of the Niger Delta.

The forum said it remained non-partisan and was not aligned with any political party or presidential candidate.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The National Chairman of PANDEF, Amb Godknows Igali, stated this while addressing journalists after a meeting of the organisation attended by former governors, former ministers, traditional rulers and other stakeholders from the six South-South states.

Igali urged the people of the region to scrutinise candidates and vote according to their conscience, stressing that their choices should reflect the development needs of the Niger Delta and the country.

He said, “PANDEF is non-partisan and not supporting any candidate. It is not a political party or support group.

We, therefore, call on the people of the South-South to exercise their civic responsibilities peacefully and vote according to their conscience, choosing candidates at all levels whose programmes, commitments, and demonstrated capacity align with the aspirations of the Niger Delta.

“I repeat, we call on the people of South-South to exercise their civic responsibility peacefully and vote according to their conscience.

“We call on our people to ‘shine your eyes’ and vote according to their conscience. They should look at candidates who have the capacity to help us as a region and move this country forward.”

The PANDEF chairman also urged Niger Delta indigenes holding public offices, particularly at the Federal Government level, to demonstrate greater commitment to the organisation’s activities.

“PANDEF calls on sons and daughters of the Niger Delta who are holding public office, especially at the level of the Federal Government, to show more commitment and interest in the activities of the organisation that are focused on uniting our people and advancing the cause of the Niger Delta.”

Also speaking, former Governor Victor Attah, who is also the Chairman of PANDEF’s Board of Trustees, said the organisation had not endorsed any candidate for the presidential election.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

“We are not aligning ourselves with any candidate. PANDEF has remained entirely neutral and non-partisan.

“As far as we are concerned, we have stated very clearly that the people of the South-South should shine their eyes and vote for whomever they believe would do their best for the Niger Delta region and the country,” he said.

This comes as political parties and presidential candidates intensify preparations for the 2027 general election.

Beyond the election, PANDEF renewed its demand for a substantial increase in the derivation allocation to oil-producing states, calling on the Federal Government to raise the current minimum of 13 per cent to 50 per cent.

Igali said the proposed increase would help address environmental pollution, infrastructure deficits and other development challenges confronting communities in the oil-producing region.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

He also called for the abolition of the onshore-offshore dichotomy in revenue allocation, arguing that oil-producing communities should receive a fairer share of the resources extracted from their environment.

The PANDEF brings together political leaders, traditional rulers and other stakeholders from Akwa Ibom, Bayelsa, Cross River, Delta, Edo and Rivers states to promote the interests of the Niger Delta.

content:
A  yet-to-be-identified motorcycle operator has been killed, and two others injured, after a speeding driver, allegedly fleeing police officers, knocked down three motorcycle riders on Liasu Road in the Idimu area of Lagos State.

The incident occurred on Saturday night during a police chase involving a vehicle suspected to belong to Internet fraudsters.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

PUNCH Metro learnt that the driver allegedly lost control of the vehicle while attempting to escape from the pursuing officers and knocked down the three motorcycle riders in the process.

One of the riders was said to have died on the spot, while the two others sustained injuries.

It was gathered that the driver and other occupants of the vehicle abandoned it and fled after realising what had happened.

An eyewitness who gave his name simply as Wahab said the vehicle was being chased from the Ile-Iwe end of the road towards the Council bus stop.

He said, “They were coming from the Ile-Iwe side when police officers in a minibus tried to stop them. It was in the process that they increased their speed and drove recklessly.

“It was when the driver lost control that he ran into the okada riders. The one directly hit died on the spot, and the driver and other male adults in the vehicle ran out of the vehicle and fled.”

The vehicle was subsequently towed to the nearest police station, while the injured victims were taken to a nearby hospital.

The incident, however, sparked a protest by commercial motorcycle riders operating along Powerline and Liasu roads, as they stopped conveying passengers to demand justice for their colleagues.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

According to another resident, Titi Jayeoba, the protest left several residents stranded as they struggled to find alternative means of transportation.

“We were stranded on Sunday after the okada riders refused to operate. People who depend on motorcycles to get to church and other places were stranded. The tricycles available could not carry everybody, so many people found it difficult to get to their destinations.

“And some were not even interested in tricycles because they would not take them into their streets,” Jayeoba stated.

It was gathered that normalcy had since returned to the area after the motorcycle operators resumed operations later in the evening.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

The deceased victim was also said to have been buried according to Islamic rites.

When contacted on Tuesday, the state Police Public Relations Officer, Abimbola Adebisi, said she was not aware of the incident. She, however, promised to revert.

title: Court orders INEC to replace NDC candidate with primary winner
excerpt: A Federal High Court in Lagos has nullified the Independent National Electoral Commission’s publication of Ibrahim Lukman as the Nigeria Democratic Congress candidate for Oshodi...
description: A Federal High Court in Lagos has nullified the Independent National Electoral Commission’s publication of Ibrahim Lukman as the Nigeria Democratic Congress candidate for Oshodi...
content:
A Federal High Court in Lagos has nullified the Independent National Electoral Commission’s publication of Ibrahim Lukman as the Nigeria Democratic Congress candidate for Oshodi/Isolo Federal Constituency I in the 2027 general election, The PUNCH reports.

In a judgment delivered on October 20, Justice Akintayo Aluko ruled that Lukman did not participate in the party’s primary election and held that INEC acted in breach of the Electoral Act 2026 by publishing Lukman’s name despite monitoring the May 29 primary at which Olumuyiwa Owadara emerged winner.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The court subsequently ordered the commission to publish the name of the winner, Owadara.

The court set aside INEC’s August 1 publication of Lukman as the party’s candidate and ordered the commission to immediately publish Owadara’s name and particulars. It also awarded N1m in costs against INEC and Lukman.

The judgment turned on INEC’s own monitoring report, which the court said showed that Owadara “scored the highest number of lawful votes cast” at the primary.

The NDC also told the court that it conducted no other primary for the constituency and that Lukman did not participate in the exercise.

Despite this, INEC published Lukman’s name and particulars as the party’s candidate, leaving Owadara off the list.
Owadara told the court that he had completed his nomination forms and had them submitted to the commission.

INEC argued that it published the names uploaded to its platform by political parties, including the NDC. Justice Aluko rejected that explanation, saying it was not supported by credible evidence.

“I am of the view that the evidence of the 1st Defendant that the names it published are the names uploaded on its platform by political parties including the 2nd Defendant is not supported or corroborated by any credible evidence,” the judge held.

The court further recorded that the NDC denied sending Lukman’s name to INEC and accused the commission of imposing him on the party, a power it said the electoral umpire did not possess under the law.

Justice Aluko held that because Lukman had not participated in the primary, INEC had no lawful basis to publish him as the party’s candidate.

“The commission has no lawful basis or justification to publish the name and particulars of the 3rd Defendant as the candidate of the 2nd Defendant for the said election,” the judge said.

He ruled that the publication amounted to “non-compliance with and brutal violation of” Sections 29(1), 32(1) and 84(1) of the Electoral Act 2026, which govern the submission of candidates emerging from valid primaries and the commission’s monitoring of party primaries.

The court also found no credible evidence that the NDC had invoked the statutory process for changing its candidate under Section 33 of the Act or conducted another primary.

“There is no credible evidence before the court to suggest that the 2nd Defendant as a political party took steps to change its candidate in line with the provision of section 33 of the Electoral Act or that another primary election was held by the 2nd Defendant,” Justice Aluko held.

He concluded that Owadara had established his case with credible evidence, adding that the primary was conducted in accordance with the party’s guidelines and constitution and the Electoral Act.

“It is my humble but firm conviction that the plaintiff has established by credible evidence that the primary election was conducted in consonance with the guidelines, constitution of the 2nd defendant and the Electoral Act and that the plaintiff emerged the winner,” he said.

The judge added that INEC’s publication of Lukman’s name “is in violent breach of the Guidelines, the Constitution of the 2nd Defendant and the relevant provisions of the Electoral Act.”

In reaching his decision, Justice Aluko relied on the Supreme Court’s ruling in Igboke v. Chukwu (2023), which set aside INEC’s publication of a candidate who had not won the relevant party primary.

Lukman had challenged the court’s jurisdiction, asking that the suit be struck out on the grounds that he was not properly served with the originating summons. He claimed he was in London when service was purportedly effected and denied that the WhatsApp number and email address used belonged to him.

The court dismissed the objection, noting that it had authorised substituted service on August 19 after the bailiff failed to serve Lukman personally. The bailiff’s affidavit stated that the processes were subsequently served through WhatsApp on August 24.

Justice Aluko found that the number used for service was the same one Lukman supplied to INEC in his Form EC9, an affidavit of personal particulars sworn to on June 27 and tendered by Owadara.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

“There is, however, credible evidence before the court to demonstrate that the 3rd Defendant is not truthful after all,” the judge said.

The court also considered WhatsApp exchanges between the lawyers to Owadara and Lukman, which it said showed that court processes were exchanged on August 27, 28 and 31. Citing the Supreme Court’s decision in Saleh v. Abah, the judge held that service on a party’s counsel who did not deny receiving the processes was valid.

The judge further noted that Lukman filed no counter-affidavit or defence to the originating summons and had therefore “failed to controvert or deny the claims and case of the Plaintiff”.

Owadara’s legal team was led by Festus Ogun, Managing Partner of FOLEGAL, with Tofunmi Adetunji and Omobola Olayanju. Ogun said the judgment had affirmed the judiciary’s role in upholding the law.

“We are most relieved that the court has demonstrated once again that it remains an impartial institution of trust which dispenses justice without fear or favour,” he told The PUNCH on Tuesday evening.

He said the team had been confident in its legal argument against the publication of a candidate who did not participate in the recognised primary.

“The last-minute announcement of an individual who never participated in the recognised primary election as a candidate is a stain on the process and institutions manning the election and a grave injustice against the legitimate winner, which should not be allowed to stand,” Ogun said.

“We are happy the court agreed with us and ordered INEC to substitute the name for our client. This is a victory for democracy”

The NDC, through its counsel, Ikechukwu Onodi, argued that INEC lacked the power to substitute a validly nominated candidate, maintaining that substitution was an internal party matter subject to statutory conditions. He also argued that the commission’s role in primaries was limited to monitoring the exercise and seeking clarification where necessary.

INEC’s counsel, Segun Bello, argued that determining whom a political party sponsors was not the commission’s responsibility and that INEC was required to remain neutral.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

On October 23, FOLEGAL wrote to the INEC National Chairman, enclosing a certified true copy of the judgment and requesting immediate compliance with the orders.

“We respectfully anticipate your earnest compliance with the said Orders of the Court,” the letter signed by Ogun stated.

title: Lagos gives residents December 31 deadline to get health insurance
excerpt: The Lagos State Government has given residents until December 31, 2026, to obtain health insurance, with enforcement of the mandatory coverage policy commencing on January 1, 2027.
description: The Lagos State Government has given residents until December 31, 2026, to obtain health insurance, with enforcement of the mandatory coverage policy commencing on January 1, 2027.
content:
The Lagos State Government has given residents until December 31, 2026, to obtain health insurance, with enforcement of the mandatory coverage policy commencing on January 1, 2027.

The Governor of Lagos State, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, stated this on Tuesday while flagging off the enforcement of mandatory health insurance under Executive Order EO/BOS/01 of 2024.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

According to a press release issued by the Office of the Special Adviser to the Governor on Media and Publicity, Sanwo-Olu also unveiled the Lagos Private Health Plans, designed to extend health insurance coverage to salaried workers and corporate organisations.

The statement said the new plans would complement the existing Ilera Eko scheme for vulnerable residents and the informal sector.

“Governor Sanwo-Olu gave every resident until 31 December 2026 to obtain insurance cover, with enforcement commencing on 1 January 2027,” the statement read.

Speaking at an event attended by government officials, health practitioners and stakeholders from the public and private sectors in Victoria Island, the governor said the objective of the executive order was to ensure that every Lagos resident had health insurance and could access quality healthcare services without financial hardship.

He said, “The ultimate objective of the Executive Order went beyond enforcement, noting that it was to ensure that every Lagos resident was covered by health insurance and could access quality healthcare services without suffering financial hardship.”

The statement added that Sanwo-Olu said every resident, employer and worker in Lagos was required to have social health insurance, noting that the executive order placed responsibilities on individuals, employers and the government.

The governor explained that while Ilera Eko catered to vulnerable residents and the informal sector, the new health insurance plans would address the needs of salaried workers and employers.

He also stressed that employers must consider workers’ healthcare a necessary cost of doing business, just as they made provisions for pensions and other employment-related obligations.

On emergency medical care, the statement said the governor emphasised that no healthcare provider should turn away residents requiring emergency medical attention because of financial constraints, stressing that patients must first be stabilised before issues relating to payment or insurance coverage were addressed.

Sanwo-Olu disclosed that 21 health maintenance organisations had endorsed participation in the new plans, describing the arrangement as a partnership between the government and private operators to expand coverage and strengthen healthcare delivery.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

title: FG kicks off $100m Southeast gas pipeline project
excerpt: …As SEDC seals deal with GasSync, commits $3m
description: …As SEDC seals deal with GasSync, commits $3m
content:
…As SEDC seals deal with GasSync, commits $3m

.. Tinubu says S’East must rise from potential to reality

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

…Mbah, governors hail Tinubu, pledge support for 400km pipeline

The Federal Government, through the South East Development Commission (SEDC) has kicked off a $100 million gas distribution pipeline project to boost industrialisation, attract investments and create jobs in the South East.

The 400-kilometre pipeline, designed to connect gas resources to industrial and commercial centres across Enugu, Anambra, Imo, Abia and Ebonyi states, has about 150 potential customers identified, with projected demand of 254 million standard cubic feet of gas per day.

The investment agreement for the project was signed on Tuesday at the South-East Gas Infrastructure Investment and Project Development Ceremony held at Hotel Presidential, Enugu, marking a significant step towards establishing a regional gas distribution network.

Tinubu, represented by the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, described the project as a strategic investment that would connect the region’s natural gas resources to industries, strengthen manufacturing and unlock economic opportunities across the five states.

“The Southeast’s entrepreneurial spirit is one of Nigeria’s greatest economic assets. I have always believed that the prosperity of the Southeast is inseparable from the prosperity of Nigeria,” the President said.

He said the project aligned with his administration’s commitment to building an integrated regional economy, stressing that gas infrastructure should support industrial development across state boundaries rather than serve isolated markets.

“Gas infrastructure must therefore serve industries and markets, not stop at political boundaries. That is the economic logic of regional integration,” he said.

The President said the pipeline would benefit manufacturers in Aba, strengthen industrial clusters in Nnewi and Onitsha, attract productive enterprises to Enugu, expand agro-processing and manufacturing in Ebonyi and connect Imo’s gas resources to the wider regional economy.

He, however, said the ambition extended beyond supplying existing factories to creating the conditions for new industries, industrial parks and investments that had stalled because of unreliable energy supply.

“Our ambition is not simply to deliver gas to existing factories. It is to make possible factories that do not yet exist, industrial parks yet to be developed, and investments that have remained on the drawing board because reliable energy was unavailable,” Tinubu said.

He described the South-East Development Commission (SEDC) as an institution established to deliver measurable development outcomes, urging it to assess its performance by the investments it mobilised, infrastructure it enabled, opportunities it created and lives it improved.

The President said the South-East Vision 2050 development framework, supported by Vice-President Kashim Shettima and the governors of the region, provided a foundation for coordinated economic growth.

He also cited his approval of the South-East Investment Company as part of efforts to attract private capital into strategic development projects, noting that governments could not finance every development ambition from public funds.

“This is the model I expect from our development institutions: identify strategic economic opportunities, prepare credible projects, commit public resources responsibly and mobilise private capital at a scale government budgets alone cannot achieve,” he said.

Tinubu commended the SEDC for committing $3 million to the gas project and establishing a framework to mobilise additional investments from state governments, institutions and private investors.

He said the project’s initial phase required approximately $100 million, describing the partnership between public institutions and private investors as essential to developing sustainable infrastructure.

“We are not investing in pipelines for their own sake. We are investing in the industries, businesses and jobs those pipelines will make possible,” the President said.

He urged the commission and its partners to uphold commercial discipline, transparency, environmental responsibility, community engagement and the highest safety standards throughout the project’s implementation.

“The true measure of government’s commitment is not what we promise, but what we deliver,” he said, expressing optimism that the investment would help create an industrial economy capable of competing in African and global markets.

Tinubu said the ultimate objective was to translate the region’s natural resources into productive economic activity, employment and improved living standards.

“Let the gas beneath our soil power our industries. Let that energy become production. Let production become employment. Let employment become prosperity for our people,” he said.

The President urged the SEDC, state governments and project partners to establish clear implementation timelines, measurable milestones and regular progress reports, stressing that the project’s success would ultimately be measured by its ability to attract investments, revive industries, create jobs and improve the economic fortunes of people across the five Southeast states.

Enugu State Governor, Dr. Peter Mbah, commended Tinubu for establishing the SEDC, describing the commission as the institutional vehicle needed to realise the Southeast’s longstanding industrialisation aspirations.

“Tinubu loves the Igbo. The SEDC is a commission whose time has come. It was an idea conceived many decades ago, but it took President Tinubu to establish this long-awaited dream of industrialisation of the Southeast,” Mbah said.

He described the signing of the investment agreement as the commencement of the investment process, adding that the initiative would help realise the region’s aspiration for a common market and coordinated industrial development.

“What we have just signed here today is an investment agreement, meaning that investment has commenced,” he said.

Mbah, who said he was excited that the project was advancing less than 13 months after he publicly advocated the idea, praised the commission for adopting an innovative financing model that brings governments and private investors together.

He said the project would create opportunities for young people to build their futures in the Southeast rather than migrate to other parts of the country in search of jobs.

“Before now, it was our young people running out of the region in search of greener pastures. But with what we have now, our young people can sit back and find their future here in the region. This is all thanks to President Tinubu,” he said.

The governor assured the SEDC and its partners that the Southeast governors were committed to the pipeline project, promising to expedite right-of-way arrangements and environmental impact assessment approvals.

“We, the Southeast governors, are committed to this. We will ensure that the right of way and EIA are given accelerated approval,” he said.

Imo State Deputy Governor Lady Chinyere Ekomaru, who represented Governor Hope Uzodimma, commended Tinubu and the SEDC for initiating the project, noting that Imo’s substantial natural gas resources placed the state in a strategic position to benefit.

She said the project was coming at an opportune time, particularly as companies were seeking to become offtakers of gas from the Assa North–Ohaji South development.

Ekomaru urged residents to consider the Federal Government’s infrastructure investments in the Southeast in making their political choices ahead of the 2027 general elections.

“A vote for APC is a direct vote for the continuation of this project. A bird in hand is worth more than 10 in the bush. Let’s reason wisely,” she said.

Anambra State Deputy Governor Dr Onyekachukwu Ibezim, representing Governor Chukwuma Soludo, commended the commission but stressed that its success would ultimately be determined by its impact on the people.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

“We will clap for you when we begin to feel the impact of what you are doing,” he said.

Ibezim noted that states across the region had gas resources that could support industrial growth if properly developed. He urged communities along the pipeline route to embrace the project and cooperate with its promoters.

“I want to urge the communities through which the pipelines will pass to have a buy-in. We are strongly behind the commission,” he said, while commending the enthusiasm shown by industrialists at the event.

Ebonyi State Deputy Governor Mrs Patricia Obila, representing Governor Francis Nwifuru, described energy as fundamental to industrial growth, lamenting that inadequate power supply had contributed to the decline of several enterprises in the region.

“Energy is power. Its importance cannot be overemphasised. With it, factories will produce, the economy will blossom and employment will be great,” she said.

Obila expressed the Ebonyi government’s readiness to support the project, promising to provide the necessary cooperation to facilitate its implementation and help moribund companies resume operations.

“We will give you all the support needed to operate in Ebonyi to ensure that our moribund companies return back to operations,” she said.

Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Regional Development, Dr Mary Ogbe, said the SEDC was developing initiatives capable of improving living standards across the Southeast.

She assured the governors that the commission would complement their development efforts rather than compete with them, while urging investors to take advantage of the opportunities emerging from the project.

Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of SEDC, Mark Okoye, said the commission had conducted technical, financial and legal due diligence before committing funds to the project, which received approval from its governing board.

Okoye said the commission was targeting aggregate regional investment participation of up to $30 million, including its initial $3 million commitment, as part of efforts to mobilise the private capital required to advance the project.

He said the initiative aligned with the commission’s industrialisation programme and its commitment to developing infrastructure that would benefit the entire region.

Representing GasSync, the project promoter, Callistus Mba said the pipeline would connect gas resources close to the Southeast to industrial users across the five states, reducing dependence on the expensive transportation of compressed natural gas (CNG) and liquefied natural gas (LNG) by road.

Mba said the proposed network would originate from the Ohaji area of Imo State, run through Owerri and branch towards Aba in Abia State and Onitsha in Anambra State, with extensions to Enugu and Ebonyi.

He said the company planned to begin construction at two points simultaneously to accelerate delivery, following concerns raised by Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah that constructing the entire network sequentially from Imo could delay gas supply to other states.

“We are going to start at Ohaji and Onitsha at the same time,” Mba said, explaining that the approach would allow construction towards Enugu and Ebonyi to progress alongside work on the Imo and Anambra sections.

He said the company had identified about 150 prospective customers across the region and was engaging industries to secure demand for the gas, including manufacturing companies, power-generation facilities and agro-processing businesses.

Mba cited Geometric Power in Abia State among the companies with which engagement was already underway. He added that the pipeline would support efforts to revive moribund industries in Enugu and develop agro-processing facilities in Ebonyi.

On the project timeline, he said procurement activities had commenced, funding arrangements were advancing towards financial close, and preparations for engineering, procurement and construction were progressing.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

“We intend to start construction in the first quarter of 2027,” Mba said, projecting that the project would be ready for first gas delivery in the second quarter of 2028, subject to the completion of the necessary requirements.

He identified regulatory approvals, right-of-way arrangements, community engagement and coordination among federal and state authorities as critical to meeting the schedule, urging the governors and relevant institutions to facilitate permits and work with host communities along the pipeline route.

title: Ofala festival: From royal dancing to robust community enterprise
excerpt: •As Obi of Onitsha warns S-East against electoral apathy•Says it will deepen political marginalisation of the regionBy Vincent Ujumadu
description: •As Obi of Onitsha warns S-East against electoral apathy•Says it will deepen political marginalisation of the regionBy Vincent Ujumadu
content:
•As Obi of Onitsha warns S-East against electoral apathy•Says it will deepen political marginalisation of the regionBy Vincent Ujumadu

The 2026 annual Ofala festival of Onitsha, Anambra State, has ended in the ancient kingdom with the usual assemblage of who is who from within and outside Nigeria. The magnificent Ime Obi arena was as expected filled to capacity by gaily dressed indigenes and their guests, as well as politicians from the various political parties, the clergy and security operatives.For effective crowd control during the Ofala, the popular Awka road from the Borromeo roundabout to the DMGS roundabout, was closed to traffic for most of the day and traffic diverted to other parts of the commercial city. The highlight of the day was the Royal dance of the Obi of Onitsha, Igwe Alfred Nnaemeka Achebe, accompanied by Ndi Ichie (cabinet chiefs).For over 500 years, the people of Onitsha have consistently shown resilience in showcasing their rich culture and tradition to the admiration of other kingdoms of the world. And for the last 15 years, communication giants, Globacom, has been part of the Ofala Onitsha and had helped to introduce some glamour into the festival.From 2025 when the theme of the celebration was “njiko na ntachi” (unity and resilience), to the 2026 theme which moved forward to “iga n’iru” (deliberate progress), the charge has always been that the people should use their craft to advance their communities and build a prosperous Onitsha Kingdom.At every Ofala, the people usually look forward to the Royal message delivered by the Obi of Onitsha. This year’s message was spectacular because, apart from speaking on the ‘State of the Nation’, which dwelt on the importance of free and fair election in 2027 and encouragement of the people of the South East to participate effectively in the election, the reigning Monarch, Igwe Alfred Nnaemeka Achebe, briefed his subjects on the Onitsha Advancement Foundation, OnAF, which came into existence five years ago, as well as other important areas affecting Onitsha.In the past one year, according to Igwe Achebe, the OnAF implementation committee approved some projects, including household farming, basic ICT training for women, one youth 2 skills programme, medical insurance, among others.In the Royal message, Igwe Achebe announced that all legal documentation and registration of the Onitsha Millennium Development Foundation, OMDF, have been completed and banking relationships established. So, Ofala Onitsha is not just about dancing, but also a forum to discuss the business and welfare of the people.Hear Igwe Achebe: “As at 31st August, 2026, total inflows of money stand at N291.78 million, comprising levies of N270.6 million, fines and penalties of N17.28 million and interest of 1% representing title ceremonies of over 24 months. This figure represents the amount paid into the Onitsha account.“Of this, N191.78 million has been reconciled and transferred to the account managed by the OMDF, while the balance of N100 million is undergoing reconciliation and will be transferred shortly. Investment activities have commenced in safe, secure and liquid money market infrastructure, and the Foundation has taken decisions to commence development activities”.According to him, going forward, the Foundation will be the sole repository for all Community funds, including the Ofala proceeds currently committed to ongoing capital projects at Ime Obi and Okwu Eze Umuezearoli and Okebunabo, adding that it will also be disbursed annually for the recurrent expenditure, such as Ime Obi maintenance and administration, vigilante security and OnAF.Beating his chest on the progress being made by Onitsha as a community, Igwe Achebe, who will be 25 years on the throne of Ezechima next year said: “The energy and commitment of our indigenes within and outside the homeland, including those abroad, are unrivaled. I am very proud that we are striving together at great sacrifice to our personal circumstances to leave Onitsha better than we inherited it.“We have a duty to nurture and grow our youths of today to grow and be ready to inherit the almost 600 legacy bequeathed by our predecessors. We are in a marathon, not a sprint. I therefore call on all indigenes, friends and associates of our community, not to relent in the sustained effort to take Onicha Ado ni’du to higher levels.”

---

content:

…My life and the lives of my children are in grave danger, now a fugitive, she cries out

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context



---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

A widow, Mrs. Njideka Ngwutu, from Nsokkara community in Ezza South Council of Ebonyi State, experienced the worst embarrassment of her life and indeed the height of encroachment into her fundamental rights, when a group of women from her community announced that she was from the community for allegedly questioning the change of the women’s meeting venue.She alleged that the leadership nd members of the Acharaukwu Development Union Women Wing (ADU) wrongfully accused her and ostracized her even without fair hearing and proper investigation. According to her, the punishment was initiated by notable personalities in her kindred to allegedly banish her and grab her late husband’s land and confiscate other estates belonging to the family.The widow has appealed to the Ministry of Women Affairs, the Governor’s wife, and other well meaning people across the country to urgently wade into matter and conduct a thorough investigate into her plights.In her letter of appeal, titled: “Urgent Petition against Extreme Harassment, Ostracization, and Attempted Forcible Eviction by the leadership and members of the Acharaukwu Development Union, Women Wing (ADU), in Ezza South Local Government Area”, the widow alleged that members of Umunaza kindred united against her because she was married from Achina Aguata Council of Anambra State and has no one to speak on her behalf because all the adult male children of her husband’s family had died of strange diseases.“I am originally from Achina, Aguata LGA of Anambra State, but was married into the Ngwuta Anyigor family of Acharaukwu Nsokkara in Ezza South LGA about 27 years ago. The union is blessed with three children. Tragically, my husband is deceased, just like his brothers, parents, and other prominent male relatives. Since the demise of my husband and his male relatives, nobody represents the family at kindred level that is why we have been maltreated.“I have been subjected to relentless torment by certain members of our kindred, Umunaza Kindred of Acharaukwu Nsokkara, who are hell-bent on dispossessing my family of the lands belonging to us.“My late husband had 2 brothers who got married and had children before the 3 brothers incidentally died under suspicious circumstances, leaving me and my co-wives as young widows with our young children behind. My parents in-law are also deceased, and so the entire Ngwuta Anyigor family was left in the hands of widows and young children. Before my mother-in-law died in 2016, my co-wives and their children had left the village owing to numerous spiritual attacks and unexplainable deaths in the family, leaving only my mother-in-law, myself, and my 3 children behind.“I had wanted to run away with my children from the village but I could not leave my mother in-law alone as she was old and needed care. I stayed behind and took care of her until she died and was buried. After her death, I realized that leaving the village with my children would mean that everyone in the family had run away and that would lead the family name, compound and legacy into extinction. I stayed back with my children, farmed on our lands and used the proceeds to train my children in school. As a result of my stay in the village, some of my husband’s nephews and nieces have returned and now live with me in the family compound,” she narrated.Mrs. Ngwuta, however, revealed that ever since she lost her husband and decided to stayed back with her children the husband’s nephews and nieces, some members of her late husband’s kindred, Umunaza, have been trying to forcefully take over her husband’s Estates and family lands and frustrate them out of the family compound.She expressed surprise that those at the forefront of the land-grabbing were close to her husband while he was alive.“Despite my vulnerability as a widow without adult male backing me in the family, I have consistently resisted these land-grabbing attempts. At the forefront of this oppression are some very close family members of my late husband, who share the same kindred with my late husband. When they attempted to forcefully take over my lands, I stood my ground, and the entire Acharaukwu community intervened, looked into the matter, and rightfully decided in my favour”Mrs. Ngwuta said, “Following their inability to take over the lands, these people have resorted to character assassination and blackmail.”“Sometime in 2024, two young girls from the same Acharaukwu Nsokkara came to my house around 9pm and begged me to agree that I had sold some cassava to them. I immediately suspected that I was being set up by the same people who had been trying to take me out of my family and I quickly refused and asked them to leave my house. Owing to my fear of being set up in more unsuspecting events, I made a conscious decision to stop attending public events or gatherings held at private residences.“This union conducts its meetings in each village from time to time, while the Annual General Meeting is held in August of every year. My own village is Effium, Acharaukwu Nsokkara, and the meeting is usually held at the Effium Playground. It is also worthy of note that as of 2024, I was the Secretary of the Effium Unit of the Union.Surprisingly, about 3 years ago, the then Chairlady of the Effium Unit of ADU Women Wing relocated the meetings from the public playground where such meetings were always traditionally held, directly to the compound of one of my late husband’s relatives. Understanding the clear danger this posed “to my safety and liberty, I protested and formally informed the association that I would not attend any meeting in anyone’s compound. I expressed my legitimate fear of being set up and subjected to jungle justice for crimes I did not commit”“Rather than understanding my plight as a fellow woman and a widow, the ADU Women Wing leadership became infuriated. They went as far as reporting me to the Catholic Church where I worship. In an attempt to make peace, the Catholic Women Organization (CWO) of my church mandated me to apologize to the ADU women.“In obedience to the CWO, I went with some members of the church to see the ADU women at Dr. Kelvin Nwankwo’s compound, but we were turned down at the gate, and Dr. Nwankwo specifically warned that they should not enter into his compound. I went back with the other church members, informed the CWO and the Priest of the church and have since then maintained my resolution not to attend such meeting in anyone’s compound”“They forcefully handed me a matchbox, indicating that I had been ostracized from the community. Furthermore, they passed the following draconian and illegal edicts against me: that I have been completely banned from fetching water from any of the community streams or boreholes, forbidden from interacting or associating with anyone in the community, and banned from entering the markets to buy or sell anything.“They (allegedly) expicitly threatened that I would be killed if I dared disobey their orders. It is abundantly clear that this women’s group is being sponsored and weaponized by some people in Acharaukwu Nsokkara whose aim is to frustrate, humiliate, and terrorize me into abandoning my late husband’s home so they can finally take over my family’s land”At the moment , “my life and the lives of my children are in grave danger. My three children, my husband’s nephews and nieces, have fled our home for fear of being harmed. I am currently living as a fugitive, sleeping in neighboring communities because it is no longer safe for me to sleep in my own marital home.”Mrs Ngwuta further alleged that one of her neighbours, Miss Rebecca Aleke, who visited her compound after she was ostracized, was later tortured and almost beaten to death for associating with her. Such action, she said, had left her traumatized and afraid of what may happen next.She is therefore calling on the wife of the Governor of Ebonyi State, Mrs. Uzoamaka Nwifuru, as her last resort to wade in and save her life and her home.“I also want Her Excellency to use her good office to promptly summon the leadership of the ADU Women Wing, Acharaukwu Nsokkara, to explain their justification for ostracizing a widow like me, denying me access to basic amenities, and issuing death threats against me”, Mrs. Ngwuta appealed.When contacted, President of the ADU Women’s Wing, Mrs. Leticia Ngele and Mrs. Eucheria Nwandende, confirmed that Mrs. Njideka Ngwuta was ostracized by the union, saying that Mrs. Ngwuta had always been at the forefront of carrying out barbaric act against other women who defaulted.However, the traditional ruler of Nsokkara Autonomous community, HRH Eze Festus Ifesinachi Okonkwo, and a major stakeholder from the Community, chief Celestine Ekechi, condemned the action of the women’s group, noting that such a barbaric act was never part of their culture.Okonkwo admitted that he was aware of the case but noted that all efforts to resolve it proved abortive, as even the letter of summons sent to the women was not honored.Meanwhile, Ezeogo Festus Okonkwo has disbanded the leadership of Acharaukwu Development Union (ADU) Women Wing for reprehensible action against the widow.Ezeogo Okonkwo, who has submitted the ban order to the office of the Honorable Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Matters, said the action of the women’s group contradicts Section 002 of the 2018 Ebonyi State Law Against Persons Prohibition (VAPP LAW)The Traditional Ruler who visibly frowned at the injustice meted out to the indigent widow, ordered that Mrs. Njideka Ngwuta should as a matter of urgency return to her matrimonial home and reunite with her children and loved ones. He warned that any further threat to her life shall be viewed seriously and visited with the full weight of the law of Ebonyi State and the Federal Republic of Nigeria.He emphasized that the barbaric act was against the culture, custom and traditions of Nsokkara and Ezza Ezekuna people noting he is very annoyed with the leadership of the women for bluntly and flagrantly refusing to honour his invitation when he got the wind of the matter.“The action, harassment and the inhuman treatment meted out against Mrs. Ngwuta is a violent act which has caused her physical and emotional trauma and is condemned in its entirety as it is an action perpetrated against her fundamental human rights and equally violates the provisions of Ebonyi State Violence Against Persons Prohibition No.002 of 2018 (VAPP LAW)”, he stressed, assuring that the palace has initiated an in-depth investigation to unravel the sponsors of the barbaric and heinous act in the community.

title: More than a slip: Dangers of falls in old age
excerpt: Renowned nationalist, lawyer, statesman and first Premier of the old Western Region, Chief Obafemi Awolowo died in the bathroom of his Ikenne home on May 9, 1987. Although the e...
description: Renowned nationalist, lawyer, statesman and first Premier of the old Western Region, Chief Obafemi Awolowo died in the bathroom of his Ikenne home on May 9, 1987. Although the e...
content:
Renowned nationalist, lawyer, statesman and first Premier of the old Western Region, Chief Obafemi Awolowo died in the bathroom of his Ikenne home on May 9, 1987. Although the exact circumstances of his death were never officially established, some have speculated that the 78-year-old elder statesman may have slipped while taking his bath.

Whether or not that was the case, his death reminds us of a reality often overlooked in Nigeria: falls are a major health threat facing older adults.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Studies from Spain, Italy and Brazil consistently show that between one-quarter and one-third of adults aged 70 years and above experience at least one fall each year. Nigerian studies have reported prevalence ranging from about 23 per cent to more than 40 per cent, depending on the community studied.

Why do older people fall?

Ageing can bring changes in balance, gait and muscle strength, making it easier to lose one’s footing. But falls are rarely caused by age alone. Arthritis, poor vision, dizziness, chronic pain and other medical conditions can increase the risk. So can environmental hazards such as slippery floors, poor lighting and uneven walkways.

A study at Irrua Specialist Teaching Hospital, Edo State, identified several risk factors among participants, including smoking, chronic medication use, musculoskeletal pain, geriatric depression, environmental hazards, cognitive impairment and abnormal gait and balance.

Researchers have also documented falls occurring during everyday activities such as bathing, lifting firewood, clearing farmland, climbing onto a motorcycle, crossing a drainage channel or pothole, standing in church or a bank, sitting down, lying down and simply walking.

The environment matters greatly. One study found that older adults living in homes free of environmental hazards were about 2.5 times less likely to experience a fall than those living in hazardous environments.

The consequences can go far beyond a bruise or cut. Falls can cause hip fractures, head injuries, prolonged hospitalisation, disability, loss of independence and premature death. Some older adults who survive serious falls never regain their previous level of mobility.

There is also a psychological consequence. Fear of falling again can cause an older person to reduce physical activity. This may lead to muscle weakness, social isolation and an even greater risk of another fall.

Preventing falls therefore requires more than telling older people to “be careful”. Family members, caregivers, communities and healthcare workers all have roles to play.

Doctors should pay attention to conditions that can increase fall risk, including sudden drops in blood pressure when standing, gait and balance problems, vision disturbances, environmental hazards and episodes of loss of consciousness.

Families can also make homes safer by clearing walkways, improving lighting, reducing slippery surfaces and ensuring that bathrooms and stairways have appropriate support.

Older adults who experience dizziness, unsteadiness, new weakness or repeated falls should tell a healthcare professional rather than simply avoiding activity. Medication may need review, while problems with vision, hearing, balance or blood pressure may require attention.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Staying physically active is also important. Appropriate walking, strength and balance exercises can help maintain muscle strength, coordination and confidence. For people who already have significant balance problems, exercise should be guided by an appropriate health professional.

Nigeria has policies intended to improve the welfare of older persons, including the National Policy on Ageing and provisions of the National Health Act. But implementation remains a challenge, and fall prevention deserves greater attention as the country’s population ages.

A fall is often treated as an accident. But for an older person, it can be the beginning of a long period of disability. That is why prevention deserves attention before the first fall occurs.

Helping older Nigerians remain safely on their feet is also helping them remain independent, active and dignified.

Watch medications: Some medicines used for blood pressure, arthritis and insomnia can cause dizziness or a sudden drop in blood pressure. Report dizziness or unsteadiness to a healthcare professional so medicines can be reviewed where necessary.

Make the environment safer: Clear walkways of clutter, loose rugs and extension cords. Pay particular attention to slippery bathroom floors. Improve lighting along dark corridors and staircases, and consider safety bars and handrails where appropriate.Wear suitable footwear: Avoid high heels, floppy slippers and shoes with slippery soles. Sturdy footwear with a secure fit and non-slip soles can provide better support.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Check vision and hearing: Poor vision, cataracts, glaucoma and hearing problems can contribute to falls. Regular checks can help identify problems that need attention.

Keep moving: Fear of falling should not automatically lead to inactivity. Walking, strength and balance exercises can help maintain muscle strength, coordination and confidence. Older people with significant balance problems should seek appropriate professional guidance before starting a new exercise programme.

The pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation, Afenifere, has constituted a committee to plan the funeral of its late national leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, who died at the age of 100.

The decision was taken on Tuesday at a meeting of the organisation’s National Executive Committee held at the residence of the deceased in Akure, the Ondo State capital.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The meeting also extended condolences to the family and reaffirmed Afenifere’s commitment to preserving the values and ideals that defined the late elder statesman’s life.

The Chairman of the National Executive Committee, the Olu of Ilu-Abo, Oba Olu Falae, said the committee would work with the family’s burial committee and the government committee to ensure a befitting burial for Fasoranti.

Oba Falae said the committee would comprise Afenifere members and representatives of other groups that had previously met at Ogbo in Ogun State, adding that its membership would be expanded.

The committee members include Oba Olu Falae, Oba Oladipo Olaitan, Bashorun Sehinde Arogbofa, Senator Femi Okurounmu, Senator Kofo Akerele-Bucknor, Chief Supo Shonibare, Archbishop Ayo Ladigbolu, Chief Tola Mobulurin, Otunba Dr Samuel Ibikunle, Chief Korede Duyile, Chief Femi Aluko and Dr Segun Mimiko.

Others are Otunba Gbenga Daniel, Dr Gbola Adetunji, Hon. Wale Oshun, Otunba Iyiola Omisore, Chief Pekun Awobona, Engr. Bayo Adenekan, Chief Lekan Alabi, Abagun Kole Omololu, Dr Akin Onigbinde, SAN, Prof. Akin Onigbinde, Chief Dare Babarinsa, Dr David Atte and Chief Ayo Abereoran.

The list also includes Hon. Lanre Omisore, Chief Sola Ebiseni, Otunba Deji Wellington, Mrs Nike Olujembola, Mrs Oluwatoyin Falade, Comrade Jare Ajayi, Arc. Goke Omigbodun and Chief Ademola Folarin.

The organisation cautioned against discussions about who would succeed Fasoranti, describing such conversations as premature and contrary to Yoruba cultural values.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

According to Oba Falae, the immediate priority is to give the late leader a befitting burial, after which a credible successor would emerge to lead the organisation.

He said the meeting stressed the need for unity among the groups involved in the funeral arrangements, adding that succession discussions should not distract from efforts to honour the deceased.

Speaking on behalf of the family, Pa Fasoranti’s younger sister, Olori Rachel Falae, described him as a quiet, disciplined and trustworthy leader whose integrity earned him the respect of the people of Akure.

She said her late brother demonstrated remarkable dedication while combining his responsibilities as a local government chairman and school principal.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

On the funeral arrangements, Olori Falae said the family expected representatives of Afenifere, members of the Akure community and the church to participate in the ceremonies.

title: Dangote Refinery IPO Attracts Investors From 120 Countries, All 54 African Nations
excerpt: Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals says its initial public offering (IPO) attracted investor applications from 120 countries, including all 54 African nations, follow...
description: Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals says its initial public offering (IPO) attracted investor applications from 120 countries, including all 54 African nations, follow...
content:
Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals says its initial public offering (IPO) attracted investor applications from 120 countries, including all 54 African nations, following the close of the offer on Tuesday.

The company described the outcome as a milestone for African capital markets, saying the offer brought together investors across all six inhabited continents and opened up ownership of a major industrial asset to a wider pool of participants.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

In a statement, President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, said the response demonstrated Africans’ willingness to invest in industries built on the continent and share in their growth.

“To have investor applications from all 54 African countries is deeply significant to me. It shows our people don’t just want to consume what Africa produces; they want to invest in it, own it, and share in its future. This is the Africa we have always believed in,” he said.

Dangote said the public offer was intended not only to raise capital but also to broaden participation in the refinery’s ownership.

“We did not undertake this IPO simply because we needed to raise capital. We wanted to open the doors of ownership, give ordinary Africans an opportunity to participate in an enterprise of global significance and establish a new culture of shared prosperity,” he said.

He added that the company would continue to pursue its expansion programme and Vision 2030 strategy, with a focus on operational performance and Africa’s energy security.

Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals, David Bird, said the international response reflected confidence in the refinery’s scale, operating capabilities and long-term prospects.

“The successful conclusion of this IPO is a remarkable milestone for Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals. Investor applications from 120 countries demonstrate extraordinary international interest in our business and the confidence investors place in this refinery’s future,” Bird said.

He said the refinery would focus on translating its industrial capacity into operational excellence, sustainable growth and long-term shareholder value.

The offer opened on September 14, with 4.1 billion ordinary shares priced at ₦525 each, representing a proposed capital raise of approximately ₦2.15 trillion.

Originally scheduled to close on October 13, the offer was extended to October 27 following approval by the Securities and Exchange Commission, giving investors additional time to participate.

According to the company, the offer was supported by commercial banks, stockbroking firms, fintech platforms, capital market institutions and other distribution partners. Their involvement provided multiple channels for eligible investors to submit applications.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Dangote Industries Limited Group Chief Financial Officer, Murat Erden, said the transaction demonstrated the potential for African financial institutions and digital platforms to connect investors across national borders.

“The Dangote Refinery People’s IPO represents much more than a landmark capital-raising exercise. It marks a defining moment in the evolution of African capital markets, demonstrating our continent’s ability to mobilise domestic savings, connect investors across borders and broaden ownership of strategic industrial assets,” he said.

Erden also highlighted the refinery’s financial performance, stating that it recorded $22.5 billion in revenue and $5.52 billion in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) in the first nine months of 2026.

He said the company believed the offer could serve as a model for wider retail participation and greater integration of African capital markets.

The IPO comes as the refinery pursues plans to expand its refining and petrochemical operations, strengthen its distribution network and contribute to energy security across Africa.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Located in Lagos, the refinery is one of Africa’s largest private industrial investments, established to increase domestic processing capacity and reduce reliance on imported refined petroleum products.

title: First Israeli Election Exit Polls Show Narrow Edge For Opposition

content:
The first exit polls from Israel’s elections showed the opposition bloc with a slight edge over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp as voting ended Tuesday, but still shy of an outright majority in the 120-seat Knesset.

The country’s main pollsters — Channels 11, 12 and 13 — projected the opposition bloc to win 52 or 53 seats, and Netanyahu’s bloc to win 50, although his Likud would be the largest single party in the parliament, with 24 or 25 seats.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Israeli Arab parties also made gains after their voter base turned out in high numbers. The exit polls showed the two Arab-majority groupings, Raam and the Joint List, winning 17 or 18 seats between them.

In the last election, Likud had walked away with 32 seats, enabling it to cobble together a coalition with smaller far-right parties after Netanyahu’s traditional allies balked at the corruption cases the premier was facing.

This time around, those mainstream right-wing parties, by and large, vowed to work with main challenger Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party — projected to nab 21 to 23 seats — to form an opposition coalition capable of unseating Netanyahu.

“The initial exit poll results indicate a complete lack of confidence in Netanyahu and the October 7 government,” Eisenkot said.

Israel’s current opposition chief Yair Lapid said Netanyahu’s bloc had suffered a “crushing defeat”, while left-wing leader Yair Golan said the public had “fired the Netanyahu government”.

While Raam and the Joint List do not belong to the opposition bloc, they have expressed openness to supporting it.

Tuesday’s poll was marked by high turnout, with many voters saying they saw it as pivotal for the country’s future.

The following is a party-by-party breakdown of the projected seat count in the first exit polls:

Likud, right-wing, led by Benjamin Netanyahu: 24 or 25

Otzma Yehudit, far-right, led by Itamar Ben Gvir: 6 or 7

United Torah Judaism, Ashkenazi ultra-Orthodox, led by Yaakov Asher: 6 or 7

Shas, Sephardic ultra-Orthodox, led by Aryeh Deri: 6 to 8

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Yashar, centrist, led by Gadi Eisenkot: 21 to 23

Beyahad, centre-right, led by Naftali Bennett: 12 to 14

The Democrats, left-wing, led by Yair Golan: 9 or 10

Yisrael Beiteinu, secular right, led by Avigdor Lieberman: 7 to 9

Raam, moderate Islamist, led by Mansour Abbas: 7



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

content:
The Federal Government has approved a ₦70,000 transport intervention for workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, following a conciliation meeting with the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC).

The agreement was reached at a meeting convened by the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment in Abuja on Tuesday, October 27, to address issues raised by organised labour.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Under the agreement, the government also approved the payment of peculiar allowance arrears, effective from May 1, 2026, with payments scheduled to begin in November in three equal monthly instalments.

The parties, however, failed to agree on the effective date for implementing the national minimum wage, although they agreed that the Minimum Wage Negotiation Committee would be constituted and begin meeting immediately.

The resolutions were contained in a press statement issued by the Ministry of Labour and Employment after the meeting, which was chaired by the Minister, Dr Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi, with NLC President Joe Ajaero leading the labour delegation.

On the transport intervention, the statement said the Federal Government “will pay a transport intervention of Seventy Thousand Naira (₦70,000) across all levels for a period of six (6) months, commencing from November 2026.”

On peculiar allowances, the government approved payments with effect from May 1, 2026, with the arrears to be paid in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November.

The statement also addressed outstanding allowances for health workers, stating that “Nineteen (19) months arrears of allowances for health workers will be redeemed within three (3) months with effect from December 2026.”

On hazard allowances for agricultural workers, the ministry said the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security had submitted the list of beneficiaries and the cost implications to the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission (NSIWC) for verification.

The verification is expected to be completed within two weeks, after which the commission will issue an implementation template.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

The parties also discussed the Consolidated Health Salary Structure (CONHESS) adjustment. According to the statement, NSIWC promised to complete the update of the cost implications within three weeks to enable the Presidential Committee on Salaries to decide on the adjustment.

On tax relief for workers, the statement said the issue would be taken to the National Executive Council because taxation is a statutory matter.

The meeting followed an earlier conciliation session held on October 22 and came after discussions on issues raised by the NLC’s Central Working Committee and National Executive Council.

The government and labour representatives agreed to reconvene after one month to assess the level of implementation of the resolutions.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

The meeting also called on state and local governments to participate in the intervention process and urged unions to push for implementation at their respective levels.

title: ₦1bn Fundamental Rights Suit: Court Fixes Dec 2 For Judgement In El-Rufai’s Suit Against ICPC, Two Others
excerpt: Justice Joyce Abdulmalik of the Federal High Court, Abuja,  has fixed Dec. 2 for judgment in a N1 billion fundamental rights suit filed by former Governor of Kaduna State, Nasir...
description: Justice Joyce Abdulmalik of the Federal High Court, Abuja,  has fixed Dec. 2 for judgment in a N1 billion fundamental rights suit filed by former Governor of Kaduna State, Nasir...
content:
Justice Joyce Abdulmalik of the Federal High Court, Abuja,  has fixed Dec. 2 for judgment in a N1 billion fundamental rights suit filed by former Governor of Kaduna State, Nasir El-Rufai,  against the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) and co-respondents.

Justice Abdulmalik fixed the date after lawyers to the parties adopted their processes in the case.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

When the case was called, El-Rufai’s lawyer was not in court.

Justice Abdulmalik then made an order deeming all the processes filed by the former governor adopted.

Counsel for the ICPC, Abdul Mohammed (SAN),  identified and adopted all their processes, urging the court to dismiss the suit in its entirety.

The I-G’s lawyer, ACP Ezekiel Rimamsomte, and Maimuna Lami-Shiru, Director of Civil Litigation and Public Law, who represented the AGF, equally adopted their separate processes and prayed the court to dismiss the suit.

While the proceeding was ongoing, Ubong Akpan, the ex-governor’s counsel, entered the courtroom and apologised for his lateness.

When the lawyer sought the permission of the court to allow him adopt his court’s documents, he was informed by the judge that his processes had already been deemed adopted.

Justice Abdulmalik consequently adjourned the matter until Dec. 2 for judgment.

El-Rufai is demanding N1 billion in damages against ICPC, the Inspector-General of Police and the Attorney-General of the Federation.

He filed the suit, alleging that operatives of the ICPC and the police violated his rights following the search of his Abuja house on 20 February.

He prayed the court to declare that the invasion and search of his residence at House 12, Mambilla Street, Aso Drive, Abuja, on Feb. 19 at about 2 pm by the ICPC and I-G amounts to a gross violation of his fundamental rights.

He said that it was a violation of the dignity of the human person, personal liberty, fair hearing, and privacy under Sections 34, 35, 36, and 37 of the Constitution.”

He sought an order directing the 1st and 3rd respondents (ICPC and I-G) to forthwith return all items seized from the applicant’s premises during the unlawful search, together with a detailed inventory thereof.

He also sought an order awarding the sum of N1,000,000,000.00 (One Billion Naira) as general, exemplary, and aggravated damages, among others.

Responding, in its counter affidavit, the ICPC said it received a petition against El-Rufai and, acting on the petition, it commenced an investigation, leading to the search at his residence.

It argued that its operatives acted under a valid search warrant issued on Feb. 18 and executed on Feb. 19 between 1:37 pm and 3:56 pm at 12 Mambilla Street, Asokoro, Abuja.

The commission said its officials were accompanied by personnel of the Nigeria Police Force, and that the exercise was witnessed by El-Rufai’s wife, Hadiza El-Rufai, and his son, Mohammed El-Rufai.

The ICPC, which urged the court to dismiss the suit, listed the items allegedly recovered from the residence.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

The I-G, also in his counter affidavit deposed to by Insp Ewa Anthony, argued that he had the statutory power to detect, arrest, investigate and prosecute offenders.

He argued that the search carried out at El-Rufai’s residence was executed pursuant to a search warrant issued by a competent court of law.

He disagreed with the ex-governor that the search warrant was invalid, insisting that it was a genuine court order.

According to him, the applicant is trying to use the honourable court to shield him away from the security investigation and prosecution in the court of law.

He, therefore, prayed the court to dismiss the suit in its entirety.

The AGF, in his counter affidavit filed by Lami-Shiru, denied being privy to the facts of the alleged matter.

He argued that the ICPC and I-G acted within their statutory functions.

According to him, the items seized from the applicant (El-Rufai) by the 1st and 2nd respondents were seized to enable them to conclude the investigation on the applicant.

He submitted that the suit was an abuse of court processes because the former governor had two pending suits on the same subject matter before the FCT High Court.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

The AGF, who argued that El-Rufai’s suit lacked merit as there are no legal and evidential justification to support all the claims and reliefs sought by him, prayed the court to dismiss it in its entirety.

title: NANS National Ex-Officio II, Patience Okoroafo, Raises Alarm Over Alleged Marginalization in Akwa Ibom, Calls for Intervention
excerpt: The Akwa Ibom representative at the National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS) National Executive Council, Comr. Patience Nnyenime Okoroafo, has raised concerns over what she describes as sustained marginalization, exclusion and undermining of her office in the state.
description: The Akwa Ibom representative at the National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS) National Executive Council, Comr. Patience Nnyenime Okoroafo, has raised concerns over what she describes as sustained marginalization, exclusion and undermining of her office in the state.
content:
In a report made public, Okoroafo, who serves as National Ex-Officio II at the NANS National Headquarters, accused the Office of the Special Assistant to the Akwa Ibom State Governor on Students Affairs, Comr. Wisdom Emmanuel, of repeatedly sidelining her despite her position as the state's representative at the national student leadership level.

### Dispute Over Representation and Recognition

According to Okoroafo, she emerged as National Ex-Officio II during the last NANS National Convention, becoming the only Akwa Ibom representative occupying a position at the organisation's National Executive Council.

She maintained that her office carries the responsibility of representing and projecting the interests of Akwa Ibom students within the national student leadership structure.

However, she alleged that since her emergence, her office has not received the recognition and institutional support it deserves.

She specifically questioned the repeated involvement of Comr. Dominic Ernest, her Cross River State counterpart, in student-related engagements and activities within Akwa Ibom State, arguing that such responsibilities should ordinarily fall within her representational mandate.

Okoroafo described the situation as an attempt to undermine her position and diminish the relevance of her office.

### Alleges Gender-Based Discrimination and Lack of Support

The NANS official also expressed concerns that her alleged marginalization may be connected to her gender.

Recounting her experience during the NANS National Convention, she alleged that she faced considerable difficulties as a female candidate seeking to represent Akwa Ibom State at the national level.

She further claimed that although the Special Assistant to the Governor on Students Affairs had indicated that government support would be shared between her and Comr. Dominic Ernest, she eventually received no financial assistance from the office.

According to her, this was unlike the experience of some representatives from other states who allegedly received sponsorship and support from their respective state governments.

Despite the challenges, Okoroafo said she financed her campaign through personal sacrifices and contributions from well-wishers, eventually securing victory and bringing national representation to Akwa Ibom State.

She expressed disappointment that, rather than receiving recognition following her emergence, she had continued to experience what she described as exclusion from important student-related engagements.

### Exclusion from Meeting with ARISE with Renewed Hope Leadership

Another major concern raised in the report was her alleged exclusion from a recent meeting involving frontline student leaders and the leadership of ARISE with Renewed Hope.

The meeting reportedly involved Dr. Wisdom Emmanuel, Engr. Uwem Okoko, Hon. Frank Archibong and the Honourable International Coordinator of ARISE with Renewed Hope.

Okoroafo stated that despite being in Akwa Ibom State when the engagement took place, she was neither invited nor informed about the meeting.

She also alleged that she was not briefed on the discussions or outcomes, despite her position within the NANS national leadership structure.

The controversy was further heightened by a social media explanation reportedly given by Comr. Dominic Ernest, who attributed her absence to a national assignment.

However, Okoroafo disputed that explanation, insisting that she was physically present in Akwa Ibom State on the day of the meeting.

She said the discrepancy raises questions about the circumstances surrounding her exclusion and the accuracy of statements made on her behalf.

### Addresses Allegations Concerning Dominic Ernest's Studentship

Meanwhile, Okoroafo also addressed the ongoing controversy surrounding claims circulating online about the studentship status of NANS Vice President, Special Duties, Comr. Dominic Ernest.

She stated that, to the best of her knowledge, Ernest contested the recently concluded NANS National Convention as a student of Cross River State University of Education, Akamkpa.

However, she clarified that determining or declaring his current studentship status was not within her responsibility.

Her position, therefore, was limited to the information available to her regarding his participation in the convention.

### Calls on NANS Leadership and Akwa Ibom Government to Intervene

In her appeal, Okoroafo called on the NANS National Secretariat, the Senate President of NANS, relevant authorities and other stakeholders to intervene and address what she described as the continued marginalization of her office.

She emphasized that her mandate was obtained through the votes of Nigerian students and should be respected irrespective of her gender.

She also appealed for fairness, equity, justice and inclusion within the student leadership structure.

The report was copied to Governor Umo Eno, the NANS National Global President, the NANS Senate President, the Akwa Ibom State Commissioner for Education, security agencies, NANS Zone B leadership and other relevant student leaders.

### The Bigger Question: Representation and Inclusion in Student Leadership

The controversy has brought renewed attention to questions surrounding representation, institutional recognition and inclusion within student leadership structures.

At the centre of the dispute is a fundamental question: Should an elected or conventionally selected representative be excluded from engagements relating to the interests of the constituency they represent?

As the concerns raised by Okoroafo come to public attention, clarification from the offices and individuals mentioned in the report would be important in establishing the full circumstances surrounding the allegations.

For now, Comr. Patience Nnyenime Okoroafo says she remains committed to representing Akwa Ibom students and Nigerian students at large.

**"Aluta Continua! Victoria Ascerta!!"**

content:
The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, has said that Nigeria could progress towards declaring the Ebola outbreak over under the World Health Organisation’s criteria, potentially as early as 7 December 2026, if no further confirmed or probable cases are detected.

Pate disclosed this in a post on his X page on Monday.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

He said that following the imported Ebola index patient’s medical evacuation from Nigeria today, 26 October, the government’s immediate priorities remain active monitoring of all identified contacts, prompt investigation of alerts, and strengthened readiness across our health facilities.

“If no further confirmed or probable cases are detected, Nigeria could progress towards declaring this outbreak over under WHO criteria, potentially as early as 7 December 2026,” the minister stated. “This date remains provisional, subject to NCDC and WHO validating the 42-day countdown.”

He, however, noted that “any further case would require a fresh countdown in accordance with those criteria”.

“Our teams, working with FCTA and state health authorities and our partners, remain focused on containment and preventing community transmission,” Pate said. “I ask Nigerians to remain calm, cooperate with contact-tracing teams and follow regular updates from NCDC and FMoH.”

On Sunday, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) said that the number of contacts, including health workers, linked to the patient had risen to 53.

title: [UPDATED] Ebola: Nigeria Has 54 Primary Contacts Now, Many Are In Quarantine, Says NCDC
excerpt: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) on Monday said that it has identified another contact linked to the confirmed case of the recent Ebola outbreak in N...
